:::: {.callout-note}

MOFography is tested with `numpy >= 1.20`, including the current `2.x` series. If you hit a deprecation or type-promotion warning, please open an issue with the failing `numpy` version.

::::

### Install dependencies, Add path and Use. ⏩
You can simply try out mofography after installing just the dependencies. In fact, I would recommend this approach, since mofography is still in active development

:::: {.callout-caution}
MOFography has been tested with `Python 3.10`–`3.12`; the `mgrcli` companion supports `3.8`–`3.12`. We recommend creating a fresh `Python 3.11` environment for new installs:

```bash
conda create -n mgr_env python=3.11
conda activate mgr_env
```

If you hit any issues on a different Python version, please open an issue.
::::

- Install the dependencies using conda or pip. A fresh `Python 3.11` environment is recommended but not required.
### Install Dependencies using Conda 

::: {.callout-note}
*Note: In all the steps below, feel free to replace `conda` with `mamba`, as it is much faster at resolving dependencies and installing packages. To install mamba use `conda install -c conda-forge -n base mamba`*
:::


```bash
conda create -n mgr_env python=3.11
conda activate mgr_env
```

```bash
conda install -c conda-forge pymatgen ase dask dask-jobqueue networkx scikit-image tqdm aiohttp icecream sparse scikit-learn rich trimesh pyvista plotly furl requests freud cupy
```
### Install Dependencies using Pip

if you'd like to install these dependencies using pip, the name of the `freud` package is `freud-analysis` so use this command instead

```bash
pip install pymatgen ase dask dask-jobqueue networkx scikit-image tqdm aiohttp icecream sparse scikit-learn rich trimesh pyvista plotly furl requests freud-analysis cupy
```
::: {.callout-note}
*Note*: If you are using a GPU, you can install the `cupy` package, which is a GPU-accelerated version of numpy. This will speed up the calculations significantly. If you don't have a GPU, you can exclude `cupy` from the list of dependencies.j
:::

### Clone the repo 🎎

- Clone the repo 
  Click on the green `Code` button and download the zip file. Unzip the file to get the repo folder, the path to which we can add and use. Alternatively, if you are using git, you may instead clone the repo using the following command from your terminal with git installed

```bash
git clone https://github.com/arung-northwestern/mofography.git .
```

#### Update if need be 🔄
- If you already have a cloned repo, pull the latest changes, since the package is being updated frequently
  
```bash
cd mofography
git pull
```
### Add path 🔗
- Add the path to mofography to your python path in your scripts and notebooks before you import,

::: {#56a486c0 .cell execution_count=2}
``` {.python .cell-code}
import sys
import os
sys.path.append(os.path.abspath('path_to_mofography'))
```
:::


of course, replace `path_to_mofography` with the relative path to the mofography directory on your local machine. This way we are not installing anything yet, so if there are changes to the source code, you can simply pull the latest changes using `git pull` and use them withouth having to reinstall the package everytime.

### Install the CLI companion (`mgrcli`) ⌨️

If you mostly want to run MOFography on one or many CIFs without writing a notebook, install the `mgrcli` companion. It ships the same Rust-accelerated pipeline (`dgrid_from_atoms_rust` → `do_periodic_segmentation_rust`) plus a prebuilt extension, and bundles its own dependency set so no manual install is needed:

```bash
pip install mgrcli
```

Verify the install:

```bash
mgrcli --version
mgrcli --help
```

One-shot full analysis on a CIF:

```bash
mgrcli process IRMOF-1.cif \
  --dgrid-method rust_exact \
  --vdw-radii-set bondi \
  --b rust_det \
  --pore-dia --psd --rag --types
```

To install from source (e.g. for hacking on the CLI), clone the companion repo and install editable:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/arung-northwestern/mgr_cli_py.git
cd mgr_cli_py/python_cli
pip install -e .
```

For the full flag reference, output layout, and how to drop down to the Python API when the CLI is not enough, see the [CLI Quick Start](./cli_quickstart.qmd) tutorial.

### Test the installation 🧪
- Import mofography to see if it works. There are CIF files in the `mofography/examples` folder, which you can use to test the package. For a full walkthrough of the canonical workflow, see the [Quick Start](./quick_cluster.qmd) tutorial.

::: {#e80f3e28 .cell execution_count=3}
``` {.python .cell-code}
import mofography as mgr
from ase.io import read
mat_atoms = read('path_to_mofography/examples/TestCIFs/P1-IRMOF-1.cif')
figures = mgr.quick_cluster(mat_atoms)
```
:::
